vulnerability.title: Vite build emits a DOM Clobbering gadget: cjs/iife/umd bundles resolve relative asset URLs from unvalidated document.currentScript.src

fixed_releases.verified_content: At v5.1.8 build.ts line 1097 requires document.currentScript.tagName.toUpperCase() === 'SCRIPT' before using document.currentScript.src; at v5.0.11 (build.ts 1076-1081) and v5.1.7 (line 1097) that check is absent. The change 5caa08f06 is first contained in v5.1.8 and absent from v5.0.11 and v5.1.7.

vulnerability.category_l2: DOM Clobbering to XSS: the generated cjs/iife/umd runtime trusts document.currentScript.src, so a scriptless named element such as redirects relative asset URLs to an attacker origin

description: Vite emits JavaScript asset-URL resolution code into cjs, iife and umd bundles when build.base is '' or './'. At v5.0.11 packages/vite/src/node/build.ts lines 1076-1081 define getRelativeUrlFromDocument, which generates new URL('', document.currentScript && document.currentScript.src || document.baseURI).href; the cjs (1097-1100), iife (1102) and umd (1105-1108) entries of relativeUrlMechanisms all use it. The generated code trusts document.currentScript.src without checking that the object is a SCRIPT element. When document.currentScript is null, which is the normal case for code that runs asynchronously after the parser, an attacker-controlled scriptless element with name="currentScript" and a src attribute (for example ) is returned by the document's named property lookup, so the relative asset URL resolves against the attacker's origin. A bundle that then loads a chunk or an asset URL through that runtime (for example document.createElement('script').src = assetUrl) fetches and executes attacker-hosted code, turning an HTML-injection foothold into XSS. The 5.1.8 fix 5caa08f06 adds a document.currentScript.tagName.toUpperCase() === 'SCRIPT' check before reading .src.

critical_operation.description: The helper that emits the relative asset-URL runtime. The generated expression falls back to document.currentScript.src whenever document.currentScript is truthy, with no tagName check. Because document.currentScript is null during asynchronous execution, a named element such as shadows it through the document's named property access, and the emitted new URL(relativePath, ...) resolves relative asset paths against the attacker-controlled src. cjs (1097-1100), iife (1102) and umd (1105-1108) all call this helper, and toOutputFilePathInJS (1159-1162) selects the relative mechanism for base '' or './'. The 5.1.8 fix adds document.currentScript.tagName.toUpperCase() === 'SCRIPT' before reading .src.

entry_point.description: Build-time code generation: the emitted cjs/iife/umd runtime string that is inlined into every relative asset URL expression in the bundle; the attacker-reachable execution happens in the page that hosts the built bundle.

trace.description: the cjs mechanism inlines getRelativeUrlFromDocument(relativePath) for the document branch of the bundle
the iife and umd mechanisms call getRelativeUrlFromDocument directly (umd passes umd=true)
toOutputFilePathInJS chooses the relative runtime when base is '' or './' and the build is not SSR
the emitted expression reads document.currentScript.src without checking tagName, so a named non-SCRIPT element shadows currentScript when it is null
the 5.1.8 fixed runtime requires document.currentScript.tagName.toUpperCase() === 'SCRIPT' before using .src

source_crosscheck.notes: CNA, NVD and the GitHub advisory agree on the mechanism (DOM Clobbering of document.currentScript in cjs/iife/umd bundles leading to XSS), on CWE-79 and on the 6.4 Medium CVSS 3.1 vector. The affected-range bounds differ in presentation: the CNA lumps 5.x as >=5.0.0,<5.2.14 and writes the 4.x boundary as <4.5.5, while the GHSA splits the 5.x lines (5.0.0-<5.1.8, 5.2.0-<5.2.14, 5.3.0-<5.3.6, 5.4.0-<5.4.6) and uses <4.5.4; for the v5.0.11 snapshot this entry records the GHSA 5.0.0-<5.1.8 range and the v5.1.8 fix. Only the CNA reference list (ade1d896) names a fix commit directly; the GHSA lists six per-line commits, of which 5caa08f06 is the 5.1-line commit actually released in v5.1.8. This root cause is distinct from the other vite entries: CVE-2024-31207 (dev-server server.fs.deny pattern bypass), CVE-2024-23331 (case-insensitive fs.deny) and CVE-2024-45811 (?import&raw bypassing ensureServingAccess). The sibling webpack advisory GHSA-4vvj-4cpr-p986 describes the same class of gadget in webpack, not in this repository.

independent_corrections_accepted: The CVE List v5 CNA range '>=5.0.0,<5.2.14' semver-wise overlaps the fixed release 5.1.8; the GHSA split (5.0.0-<5.1.8) is the correct 5.0/5.1 branch range, and the entry keeps the GHSA range.
The CNA patched-version list omits 5.1.8 (it lists 5.4.6, 5.3.6, 5.2.14, 4.5.5, 3.2.11); git ancestry and npm publication both confirm 5.1.8 is first patched for the 5.0/5.1 line.
The 4.x first-patched version differs between records (GHSA/OSV 4.5.4, CVE text 4.5.5); irrelevant to the 5.0.11 snapshot and not recorded as a claim.

The earlier description of CVE-2024-31207 as 'picomatch matchBase in server.fs.allow' does not match the public advisory, which describes a server.fs.deny pattern bypass for requests with directories; the distinct-root-cause conclusion is unaffected and the crosscheck wording was corrected.
The relative branch of toOutputFilePathInJS spans lines 1159-1162 (the joinUrlSegments fallback is at 1162), not 1159-1161; the trace now uses 1159-1162.
The GHSA reference list does not name 5caa08f06; it lists the sibling per-line commits. Git ancestry shows 5caa08f06 is the 5.1-branch fix between v5.1.7 and v5.1.8.

Reviewer additionally traced the sink: asset.ts renderAssetUrlInJS (lines 68-137) inlines the runtime for __VITE_ASSET__ URLs in JS output, and importAnalysisBuild.ts routes chunk/asset dependencies through the same path, so a dynamic script load of an asset URL is a plausible sink.
review.duplicate_check: Reviewer confirmed CVE-2024-31207, CVE-2024-23331 and CVE-2024-45811 are all dev-server file-serving/access-control issues, distinct from this build-output DOM-clobbering gadget, and none shares the 5caa08f06 fix.

limitations: Static verification only; no build was run, no bundle was generated and no browser or DOM was exercised.

The vulnerability is a gadget: it requires the hosting page to already contain an attacker-controlled scriptless HTML element (for example through an HTML-injection flaw or an unsanitized name attribute); it is not directly exploitable through a plain HTTP request to the Vite dev server.

The bundle must use build.base '' or './' (relative base) and the cjs, iife or umd output format for the relative runtime to be emitted; the es format uses import.meta.url and is not affected by this path.

The CNA range >=5.0.0,<5.2.14 overlaps the GHSA's per-line ranges; this entry records the 5.0/5.1 branch range (5.0.0-<5.1.8) that contains the v5.0.11 snapshot. No 5.0.x backport exists, so 5.0.0 through 5.0.13 remain affected and 5.1.8 is the first fixed release for this branch.
The CNA reference list names only ade1d896, which is a main-line commit; the commit released on the 5.1 line is 5caa08f06, identified from git ancestry and the v5.1.8 tag.
Public records disagree on the 4.x boundary (CNA <4.5.5, GHSA <4.5.4); this entry does not record a 4.x claim.
NVD is Deferred with no Primary metric and no CPE configuration; its 6.4 Medium metric is the CNA's, imported as Secondary.

The reviewer identified the concrete sink path in the toolchain: renderAssetUrlInJS (asset.ts 68-137) inlines the runtime for __VITE_ASSET__ URLs in JS output and importAnalysisBuild.ts routes chunk/asset dependencies through the same relative runtime; the claim did not originally name these call sites.

The CVE List v5 CNA range '>=5.0.0,<5.2.14' overlaps the fixed 5.1.8 release in semver terms and its patched-version list omits 5.1.8; the entry follows the GHSA 5.0.0-<5.1.8 range and the git-verified 5.1.8 fix.
open_questions: Whether a real page reachable by an attacker also loads a relative asset through the emitted runtime after the clobbered URL is resolved depends on the application's bundle; the advisory's PoC shows one such pattern (asset URL assigned to a dynamically created script element).
